questions.question: What is the safest statement about an indexed document and search visibility?
options: A successful source-database commit guarantees immediate Elasticsearch visibility
The document becomes searchable when its indexed representation is exposed by refresh
A replica makes the document searchable before the primary applies it
A snapshot controls when the document appears in search
questions.explanation: Indexing acceptance and search visibility are separate moments. Refresh publishes searchable Lucene segments; source commits, replica count, and snapshots do not eliminate that boundary.

questions.question: A product title needs relevance search and alphabetical sorting. Which mapping best matches both operations?
options: A text field only with fielddata enabled by default
A keyword field only
A text field with a keyword multi-field
An integer field
questions.explanation: The text path supports analyzed relevance queries while the keyword subfield supplies an exact value and doc values for sorting or aggregations.

questions.question: An index will contain 360 GB of primary data and has 12 primary shards. What is its average primary shard size?
options: 15 GB
30 GB
60 GB
120 GB
questions.explanation: 360 GB divided by 12 primary shards is 30 GB per primary shard before accounting for replicas or measured index overhead.

questions.question: A one-primary index has two replicas but only two eligible data nodes. What should the operator expect?
options: All three copies can share one node
One copy remains unassigned because three copies need at least three eligible nodes
The primary is split automatically into two shards
The replicas become snapshots
questions.explanation: Elasticsearch does not place a primary and its replicas on the same node. Three shard copies require at least three eligible nodes to assign every copy.

questions.question: What does yellow cluster health mean?
options: At least one primary shard is unavailable
All primaries are assigned but at least one replica is unassigned
Every primary and replica is assigned
Every query is timing out
questions.explanation: Yellow means primary data is assigned and searchable, but the requested redundancy is incomplete. Red indicates at least one unassigned primary.

questions.question: Why are replica shards not a complete backup strategy?
options: Replicas cannot serve search requests
Replicas never contain indexed documents
Replicas copy accidental deletes and bad writes, so independent snapshots or source replay are still required
Replicas are stored only in client memory
questions.explanation: Replication protects against loss of a shard copy, not logical corruption. A bad mutation is replicated, while snapshots or replayable source data provide an independent recovery point.

questions.question: Which evidence is most important before moving a read alias to a reindexed generation?
options: The new index name is shorter
Backfill and live checkpoints reconcile, document counts match, and relevance, latency, and rollback gates pass
The old index has no replicas
The cluster has received one successful query
questions.explanation: An alias cutover should prove data completeness, catch-up, product quality, performance, and recoverability. Index creation alone does not prove the new generation is safe to serve.
